newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front says wants to avoid elections.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front says wants to avoid elections.

text.p: India's defeated United Front coalition said on Sunday it wanted to avoid mid-term elections and had taken no decision on the Congress party's demand that its leader, caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, quit.

"The general view was elections should be avoided," spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters after a meeting of the coalition's decision-making Steering Committee. He said four regional parties in the alliance felt polls must be avoided.
Reddy said the four parties -- two from Tamil Nadu state, one from Andhra Pradesh and the fourth from Assam -- "expressed the view that elections must be avoided".

Deve Gowda, who resigned on Friday after losing a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament, has repeatedly said there was no alternative to going to the polls as Congress had withdrawn its support to the United Front coalition.

Congress has said it would consider helping the United Front form a new government, averting elections, provided the alliance dropped Deve Gowda as its leader. Until Sunday, the United Front Steering Committee had said there was no question of changing leaders.

Reddy said the committee had considered Congress's demand. "There were references to the changes in leadership in the context of the demand from Congress. There was no decision taken on this," he said, adding that Deve Gowda had said he would abide by the Steering Committee's decision.
